findings.title: Empty updateMany throws after every cache write
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) after upserting CalendarCache. Prisma Client rejects updateMany when data is an empty object ("Argument data needs at least one argument"), so this throws on every successful cache fill, including Google webhook refreshes and the refill at the end of unwatchCalendar. Callers that treat the throw as a sync/watch failure will retry, record errors, and can eventually stop watching the calendar even though the cache write already succeeded. An empty payload also does not reliably bump SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. The new repository method types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is not assignable to updateMany's UpdateManyMutationInput. Pass an explicit update such as { updatedAt: new Date() }.

findings.title: Cache delete does not refresh connected calendars
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (or apps.integrations). The calendar settings query lives in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper and onChanged is often omitted, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the previous Last updated time and the delete action. Users are told the cache was deleted while the UI keeps offering to delete it until a full reload.

findings.title: Cache timestamp format is a type error and ignores locale
findings.body: The last-updated label always does new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }).format(new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)). cacheUpdatedAt is Date | null | undefined, and hasCache is a separate boolean, so TypeScript does not narrow it; new Date(cacheUpdatedAt) is not assignable under strictNullChecks and should fail typecheck. The formatter is also hardcoded to en-US, so the translated cache_last_updated string still shows a US timestamp for every locale. Format only a narrowed Date with the active locale.

findings.title: Deleting cache does not stop watches that recreate it
findings.body: deleteCacheHandler only runs calendarCache.deleteMany for the credential. It does not clear Google channel fields or stop notification channels. Webhook handling calls fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, which writes CalendarCache again, so for any watched Google calendar the rows return on the next push and the delete looks like it failed. The new confirm_delete_cache string says the action cannot be undone, which is false while watches are active. Either stop watches the way unwatchCalendar does before deleting, or tell the user the cache will be rebuilt and trigger a refetch. The access check also throws a plain Error, which tRPC reports as an internal 500 instead of NOT_FOUND or FORBIDDEN.

findings.title: Cache status counts expired rows as live cache
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups every CalendarCache row for the credential and takes max(updatedAt), with no expiresAt >= now filter. Availability reads ignore expired rows, but the settings dropdown treats any truthy cacheUpdatedAt as live cache and offers Delete cached data. Credentials whose cache has fully expired still show a last-updated time. Restrict the query to unexpired rows, and return no status when every row is expired.

findings.title: Existing cache rows are stamped with migration time
findings.body: updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row gets the migration execution time rather than the last free/busy write. The new status query uses max(updatedAt), so after deploy every Google credential that already has cache will show that deploy timestamp as Last updated until the next Prisma upsert. Backfill from a closer signal (for example expiresAt minus the cache TTL) or keep legacy updatedAt null and only display a timestamp after a real update.

findings.title: Webhook helper fails on Linux and writes the wrong env file
findings.body: The script updates GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL with sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS sed and fails on GNU sed, so the env update does not work on Linux. ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the current working directory, not the script or repo root. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore targets a path outside the repo, and if that file is missing touch creates it and writes the tunnel URL there instead of the project .env. Resolve the env path from the script directory and use a portable in-place edit.

findings.title: No tests for cache delete authorization or status
findings.body: deleteCache is a new mutation that deletes CalendarCache rows after an ownership check, and getCacheStatusByCredentialIds changes what connectedCalendars returns, but there are no unit or integration tests. A dropped userId filter, deleting another user's credential, or stale cacheUpdatedAt after delete would not be caught. Cover owner success, rejection of another user's credentialId, and that connected calendars no longer report cache after deletion.
